cues.en: It's shocking. In my opinion, it's one of the most shocking things and it's perhaps the most astonishing conclusion of modern physics. We now are here. What now means? What is the meaning of now? Well, I know what is the meaning of now for me. You know what is the meaning of now for you. Is it the same now?
cues.zh: 这太震撼了。在我看来，这是最令人震惊的事情之一，也许是现代物理学中最惊人的结论。我们现在在这里。“现在”意味着什么？“现在”的含义是什么？我知道“现在”对我意味着什么，你知道“现在”对你意味着什么。但它们是同一个“现在”吗？

cues.en: Thank you. Thank you for this very kind introduction. The first thing I have to do is to pull up this, which I prepared before you came in. Let's see if it, yes, sorry. Which I'm gonna use, and that would be my high-tech technological equipment to talk about time. That would be my metaphor of time, right? Time is a long line.
cues.zh: 谢谢。谢谢大家如此热情的介绍。我首先要做的是拉起这个，这是大家入场前我准备好的。看能不能……好的，不好意思。我要用这个，这就是我用来探讨时间的高科技装备。这就是我对时间的隐喻，对吧？时间是一条长长的线。

cues.en: There is a present. There is the past, the far past, the more far past. This is 10 minutes ago. This is yesterday. This is last year. Down there is this big bang. This is tomorrow. And the future, we don't know. So this is a matter of time. We are sort of here. We have one hour, whatever, with questions and so on. So we're going to cover that. And I'm going to tell you that time is not like that.
cues.zh: 这里是现在。这里是过去、遥远的过去、更遥远的过去。这是十分钟前。这是昨天。这是去年。最下面那里是大爆炸。这是明天。未来则是未知的。所以这就是时间的比喻。我们大概在这里。我们有一个小时左右，包括提问等等。所以我们要涵盖这些内容。而我要告诉大家的是，时间并不是这样的。

cues.en: That would be the message. And so what I want to do is to give you a sense of where I think we are about understanding of this strange mysterious things which is time. It will be sort of a journey. For me, time has been an open question from
cues.zh: 这就是我想传达的信息。所以我想让大家了解一下，关于时间这个奇怪而神秘的事物，我认为我们目前的认知处于什么阶段。这会是一段旅程。对我来说，时间一直是一个悬而未决的问题，从

cues.en: my early years as an adolescent from all the way through my studying of physics and then into my work as a physicist. You know, sort of an obsession. Because quantum gravity requires us to rethink what is time, I've been going around, around, around this question. What is time? So in the book and in what I want to tell you tonight is a bit of a synthesis of that, where we are, what we know,
cues.zh: 我早期的青少年时期，一直贯穿于我的物理学习生涯，再到后来成为物理学家的工作。可以说，它成了一种执念。因为量子引力要求我们重新思考时间是什么，我一直在围绕着这个问题打转。时间到底是什么？所以在书中以及今晚我想告诉大家的，就是对这些探索的一点总结：我们处于何处，我们知道些什么，

cues.en: what we think is true, including the parts that we don't yet know, we are confused about. And I will do it as taking you to a sort of journey, which is back and forth. So I'll start from this idea of time, this long line that passes. We are here, actually we moved a little bit already, a little bit more here, and time passes. And I'll show what's...
cues.zh: 我们认为什么是真实的，包括我们尚不清楚、感到困惑的部分。我将带大家展开一段往返之旅。我会从这种时间观念开始，这条流逝的长线。我们在这里，其实我们已经移动了一点点，往这边又多了一点，时间在流逝。而我将展示……

cues.en: quite rapidly tell you what's wrong with this idea. Why this is a wrong idea about time and in which sense it is wrong. And this would be a step sort of down into more and more general views of nature where time has less and less property and loses its pieces, so to say, all the way to...
cues.zh: 很快告诉大家这种观念错在哪里。为什么这是一种错误的时间观念，以及它在何种意义上是错的。这会是一次逐步深入更具普适性的自然图景的过程，在那里，时间的属性越来越少，可以说，在一步步丢失其碎片，直到……

cues.en: What I think is the current understanding of the structure of time, which is that there is very little time in nature. And that will be the journey, the one-way journey. And then there is the journey back, which is how from this nature at the level of quantum gravity, which is sort of the bottom level of our understanding of the physical world, in sense of generality flows, how from there we get back to this time, to the time of our
cues.zh: 我认为的当前对时间结构的理解，那就是自然界中几乎不存在时间。这就是那段旅程，一段单程旅程。然后还有一段返程之旅，那就是如何从量子引力层面的这种自然——就普适性流动而言，它可以说是我们对物理世界理解的最底层——从那里，我们如何回到这个时间，回到属于我们

cues.en: our experience. So it will be a long one-way end-return trip where I want you to lose all your ideas of time to then sort of understand back where our comment I come from, right? So this is the time of our experience. First of all, it's a long line. Namely, what do I mean by a long line? It's a seek, what do we mean?
cues.zh: 我们经验中的时间。所以这将是一段漫长的往返之旅，我希望大家抛弃对时间的所有固有观念，然后再去理解我们日常的时间源自何处，对吧？这就是我们经验中的时间。首先，它是一条长线。也就是说，我所说的“长线”是什么意思？它是一个顺……我们究竟是什么意思？

cues.en: It's a sequence of moments, instant, now, before, later, which is ordered, like the English when they wait for the bus. So maybe I'm trying to Italianize you a little bit, but I don't want you to crowd for getting the next bus. That's not where I want to go.
cues.zh: 它是一连串时刻——瞬间、现在、之前、之后——有序排列，就像英国人等公交时那样。也许我是想让你稍微意大利化一点，但我不希望你为了赶上下一班公交而挤作一团。那不是我想去的地方。

cues.en: But all these instances are from a long line. They're one next to another one in a one-dimensional thing. This line has a direction, right? The past is completely different for the future. This is one of the most obvious things and the most trivial thing to say, but let me say it precisely because then I'm going to say it's not true. The past is fixed. It's given.
cues.zh: 但这些实例都来自一条长线。它们在一维的东西里一个挨着一个。这条线有方向，对吧？过去与未来完全不同。这是最明显、也最微不足道的说法之一，但让我先精确地说出来，因为接下来我要说它并不成立。过去是固定的。它是给定的。

cues.en: We remember it, we know it, we have traces of it. We have books that talk about the past. We have departments in our university that study the past, history. We don't have many departments that make historical history about the future. There are traces in nature. If you look at the moon, there are craters that are formed by storms fell on the moon in the past.
cues.zh: 我们记得它，知道它，拥有它的痕迹。我们有谈论过去的书。我们大学里有研究过去——历史——的院系。我们没有多少院系会去写关于未来的历史。自然界中也有痕迹。如果你看月亮，上面有环形山，是过去落到月球上的风暴形成的。

cues.en: So the past lists all these traces with memories in our mind. The future, there is nothing like that. There's no memory, no traces, still has to come. So that's part of this idea that we have about time. Time has a metric property. Namely, we can talk about duration of time. This chart I'm giving, this presentation is going to last 45 minutes.
cues.zh: 所以过去列着所有这些痕迹，以及我们脑海中的记忆。未来则完全没有这些东西。没有记忆，没有痕迹，尚未到来。这就是我们对时间观念的一部分。时间具有度量属性。也就是说，我们可以谈论时间的持续长度。我展示的这张图，这个演讲将持续 45 分钟。

cues.en: fixed amount of time that we measure with clocks. And we know what it means, this interval being equal to this integral, being equal to this integral, being equal to this interval, and so on. And clocks measure that. And clocks are devices that are meant to tell us where we are along this line. What time is it? Where am I? Is it already tomorrow? It's not yet tomorrow. And clocks are designed to work all together. That's the purpose of a clock.
cues.zh: 一段固定的时间，我们用钟表来测量。我们知道它意味着什么：这个区间等于这个积分，等于这个积分，等于这个区间，等等。而钟表测量的就是这个。钟表这类装置，是为了告诉我们自己在这条线上的哪里。现在几点？我在哪里？已经到明天了吗？还没到明天。钟表被设计成彼此协同工作。这就是钟表的目的。

cues.en: So if you take two clocks, you move them apart, wait a little bit, you bring them back together, they still have the same time. If they had the same time. If not, it means one clock is broken or it's not going well or something else. This is the time of our experience. Now, what's wrong with this image? First of all, there's nothing wrong, obviously, as long as we...
cues.zh: 所以如果你拿两个钟，把它们分开，等一会儿，再把它们放回一起，它们仍然显示相同的时间。前提是它们原本时间相同。如果不是，就说明有一个钟坏了，或者走得不准，或者别的什么。这就是我们经验中的时间。那么，这幅图景有什么问题？首先，显然没有问题，只要我们还……

cues.en: carry on our daily life. It's a very good construction, conceptual idea about time that works very well in our daily life. But it does not work. It stopped working when we look a little bit more far ahead. And the more we look far ahead, the more this number of
cues.zh: 继续过我们的日常生活。这是一个非常好的建构，是关于时间的概念框架，在我们的日常生活中运作得很好。但它行不通。当我们稍微往更远处看时，它就不再有效。而且我们越往远处看，这个数量就越多……

cues.en: properties that I describe about time, go away. So the main message somehow, the full talk I'm giving, is that time is not a single thing. It's this multi-layered concept that has all this property that I told you. It's one-dimensional, it's a metric, it's oriented, it's the same for everybody, it's measured by clock, and so on and so forth. This which, in our intuition, comes as a package, is time.
cues.zh: 关于时间的、我所描述的那些性质，就越会消失。所以，某种程度上，我整场演讲的主要信息是：时间不是单一的东西。它是这种多层概念，拥有我告诉过你的所有这些性质。它是一维的，是可度量的，是有方向的，对每个人都是一样的，可以用钟表测量，等等。这个在我们的直觉中作为一个整体出现的东西，就是时间。

cues.en: it's properly thought as a combination of properties that we can dismount one by one. Sometimes it's layered, or it's like a mechanism, like an engine of your scooter. You can take away one piece, the carburetor, you can take away the piston, you can take away this, you can take away that, and what remains is not the scooter. What remains is nothing at all.
cues.zh: 它其实可以被看作是一系列特性的组合，我们可以把它们逐一拆解。有时它是分层的，或者像某种机械结构，比如你踏板车的引擎。你可以拆下一个零件，化油器，你可以拆下活塞，你可以拆下这个，拆下那个，最后剩下的就不再是踏板车了。剩下的什么都不是。

cues.en: And that's going to happen with time. When you take away this, take away that, take away that, what remains is nothing at all, because time is a combination of these properties. So let's say one property is one by one. The first one, maybe I'll mention three or four of these, let's say four, to dismantle this idea of time. Some of this you might know, depending on how much physics you know or how much you've heard these stories already. Some you...
cues.zh: 时间也是如此。当你拿掉这个，拿掉那个，再拿掉那个，最后什么都不会剩下，因为时间就是这些特性的组合。那么我们就一个特性一个特性地来看。首先，我大概会提到其中的三到四个，就算是四个吧，来拆解关于时间的这种观念。其中有些你可能已经知道了，这取决于你懂多少物理，或者你之前听过多少这类故事。有些你……

cues.en: probably haven't known, some are very solid knowledge, some are things we suspect. I would say the first three are very solid knowledge, but the implications of taking all them together are strong. So first one, clocks measure time, fine, and clocks go all together at the same speed, or that's wrong. Why is wrong? Because it's a fact that if I take two clocks,
cues.zh: 可能还不知道，有些是非常确凿的知识，有些则是我们的推测。我认为前三个是非常确凿的知识，但把它们放在一起所产生的推论却极其颠覆。首先，时钟测量时间，没问题，而且所有时钟的走速都一样——错了，这是不对的。为什么不对？因为事实是，如果我拿两个时钟，

cues.en: And if I take two good clocks, and I move them apart, move one, or I bring one higher, and keep one lower, and I wait a little bit, and I move them together, if these are good enough clocks, they will indicate a different time. It's a fact, okay? It was clearly understood by Einstein 100 years ago, so in a sense we've been knowing this for 100 years, but it's recent.
cues.zh: 如果我拿两个精准的时钟，把它们分开，移动其中一个，或者把一个放得更高，另一个放得更低，然后等一会儿，再把它们放到一起，只要时钟足够精准，它们显示的时间就会不一样。这是客观事实，明白吗？爱因斯坦在100年前就完全弄明白了这点，所以从某种意义上说，我们知道这事已经有100年了，但直到最近……

cues.en: that we actually have good glocks, not these, that we can measure this. And today with atomic clocks, clocks that measure easily one part time with a narrow one in 10 to the...
cues.zh: 我们才真正拥有足够精准的时钟——不是这种——来测量出这种差异。如今借助原子钟，这种时钟测量时间的误差可以轻松达到百亿亿分之一，也就是十的……

cues.en: 18, 17, 18, even 19. This is very rapidly advancing the technology of clocks. So with these clocks, you can take two clocks at a different altitude of 40 centimeters, 50 centimeters, and measure that. So the clock up here goes faster than the clock down here. There's more time here. There's more time for thinking, for growing older, for everything.
cues.zh: 18次方、17次方、18次方，甚至是19分之一。时钟技术的发展非常迅速。所以用这些时钟，你可以把两个时钟放在相差40厘米或50厘米的不同高度，就能测出这个差异。放在上面的时钟比放在下面的时钟走得更快。高处的时间更多。有更多的时间去思考，去变老，去经历一切。

cues.en: there is more time in your head. Your head is older than your feet. Your head has, unless you have spent all your time upside down, in which case it's the other way around, okay? Why, well, why is it, it's a funny question.
cues.zh: 你的头脑经历的时间更多。你的头比你的脚更老。你的头经历了——除非你一辈子都在倒立，那样的话情况正好相反，明白吗？为什么？嗯，为什么会这样，这是个有趣的问题。

cues.en: One could say why? Well, because we know from general relativity that the earth, which is a big rock, big mass, slows down time. So mass slows down time next to it. But why, I think the right question is why not? Why is still this hard for us to digest? Because we're used to time being the same for everybody. We're used is two person have the same age and they separate.
cues.zh: 有人可能会问为什么？嗯，因为广义相对论告诉我们，地球作为一个巨大的岩石、巨大的质量体，会拖慢时间。所以质量会放慢其附近的时间。但为什么会这样？我认为真正的问题应该是“为什么不呢？”为什么我们还是很难接受这一点？因为我们习惯了时间对每个人都是一样的。我们习惯了两个人同岁，哪怕分开了也是如此。

cues.en: One goes to America, the other goes to China, and they come back after a while. They still have the same age. That's our experience. But that's not right, because they have aged differently, depending on how they moved, depending if they have lived more up or more down, and so on. In our experience, these differences are small.
cues.zh: 一个人去美国，另一个去中国，过一阵子回来。他们的年龄仍然一样。这是我们的经验。但这不对，因为他们的衰老程度不同，取决于他们怎么移动，取决于他们更多是在上方还是下方生活，等等。在我们的经验里，这些差异很小。

cues.en: and smaller than our perception of time or the precision of our watches that we carry, so we don't notice that. But if we lived a little bit in the future when I hope there will be starships going around at fast speed and coming down, we will have to confront that. So the reason for which we think the time is the same for everybody is because we used it.
cues.zh: 而且比我们对时间的感知，或我们随身手表的精度还小，所以我们注意不到。但如果我们在未来生活一阵——我希望那时会有星际飞船高速绕行并降落——我们就必须面对这一点。我们认为时间对所有人都一样，原因是我们一直这么使用它。

cues.en: We got used to it by our approximation. It's like, you know, if you grew up in the Netherlands, which is completely flat, you think that the Earth is just all at the same level. And somebody says, you know, there are some places of the Earth where the Earth goes down. We say, oh, how could this? Yeah, it's called mountains. Wow, right? You have never seen mountains, so you're surprised. We live in a...
cues.zh: 我们在近似中习惯了这一点。就像，如果你在荷兰长大，那里完全平坦，你会以为地球处处都在同一高度。然后有人说，地球上有些地方会往下走。我们会说，哦，这怎么可能？对，那叫山。哇，对吧？你从没见过山，所以你会惊讶。我们生活在一个……

cues.en: region in which this difference of time is small, so we're not used to this. If we had a big mass of black hole not far from here, we'd be used to the fact that when you go to a black hole, you come back, everybody else as much has grown older than you. Good. Which means already that this line is just wrong because the time between here and here, two events, is not fixed. It depends whether you were higher or whether we lower, for instance.
cues.zh: ……时间差异很小的区域，所以我们不习惯这个。如果附近有一个大质量黑洞，我们就会习惯这个事实：你去了黑洞再回来，其他所有人都比你老得更多。好。这已经意味着这条线是错的，因为这里和这里、两个事件之间的时间并不是固定的。比如，它取决于你是在更高处还是更低处。

cues.en: So it's not, there isn't a single time in the universe. Already there are many times. And in fact, in Einstein generativity, you don't have a single time. You have one time per every line, per every good. That's point one. Now point two that follow quite rapidly from that, which in fact something that Einstein realized even before generativity, special relativity, but it has long, take long for becoming absorbed.
cues.zh: 所以不是，宇宙中不存在单一的时间。已经有很多时间了。事实上，在爱因斯坦的广义相对论里，你没有单一的时间。每条线、每个对象都有自己的时间。这是第一点。第二点很快由此推出；事实上，它是爱因斯坦甚至在广义相对论之前、在狭义相对论里就意识到的东西，但它花了很长时间才被吸收。

cues.en: because it's shocking. In my opinion, it's one of the most shocking thing and it's perhaps the most astonishing conclusion of modern physics. Which is, we now are here. What now means? What is the meaning of now? Well, I know what is the meaning of now for me. You know what is the meaning of now for you. Is it the same now?
cues.zh: 因为它令人震惊。在我看来，这是最令人震惊的事情之一，也许是现代物理学最令人惊讶的结论。那就是：我们现在在这里。“现在”是什么意思？“现在”的含义是什么？嗯，我知道“现在”对我意味着什么。你知道“现在”对你意味着什么。这是同一个“现在”吗？

cues.en: Well, obviously yes, because I look at you, you look at me, and I say now, you say yes now, I hear yes now, so we are in the same now, right? And then wait a little bit, look, we are in a new now, so a little bit moved here, but we are together, always together the same now. But think for a moment. When we look around, if I look at you, do I see you now? Well, not really, because lights take time to come from you to me, right?
cues.zh: 嗯，显然是的，因为我看你，你看我，我说“现在”，你说“是的，现在”，我听到“是的，现在”，所以我们处在同一个现在，对吧？然后等一会儿，看，我们处在一个新的现在，所以这里稍微移动了一点，但我们在一起，总是处在同一个现在。但想一下。当我们环顾四周，如果我看你，我看到的你是现在的你吗？嗯，并不真的，因为光从你到我需要时间，对吧？

cues.en: So I see you sort of a little bit in the past. Now, time takes a few nanoseconds to come from you to me. So I see you as you were a few nanoseconds ago. Well, nanoseconds are irrelevant. But if you were on Jupiter, I would see you two hours ago. And if you were on a star, I would see you four years ago, a close star. And if you were on different galaxies in Andromeda, I would see you millions of years ago.
cues.zh: 所以我看到的你，其实是稍微过去的你。现在，光从你那传到我这需要几纳秒。因此我看到的是几纳秒前的你。好吧，几纳秒微不足道。但如果你在木星上，我看到的就是两小时前的你。如果你在一颗恒星上，一颗邻近的恒星，我看到的就是四年前的你。而如果你在仙女座的不同星系里，我看到的就是几百万年前的你。

cues.en: So I couldn't say now is when I see you. And if you look at me in the moment I see you, you are going to see me in the past, in the future for me. So between the UIC and the U that see me in the moment I see you, there's an interval between the two, which is a few nanoseconds here, but a few hours in Jupiter, and millions of years if you were in a different galaxy. Philosopher has been saying that for a very long time. Husser has been saying that. It goes back to St. Augustine, famous pages about the nature of time in his book.
cues.zh: 当我们思考时间时，很多时候我们想的不是物理上的过去和物理上的未来，而是我们在脑海中对物理过去的记忆，以及对未来的预期。哲学家们早就这样说了，Husser 曾这样说过，这甚至可以追溯到 St. Augustine，他在著作中关于时间本质的那些著名篇章。

cues.en: The Confessions, I don't know how it's translated in English. He says, when I listen to music, I get a meaning from a musical phrase, but I never listen to the phrase. I listen to one note at a time, right? If I listen to one note, how do I know about the previous notes? How do I get the meaning? Well, of course I know because I remember them.
cues.zh: 《忏悔录》，我不知道英文是怎么翻译的。他说，听音乐时，我能从乐句中领会到某种含义，但我从没完整听过这个乐句。我每次只听一个音符，对吧？如果我一次只听一个音符，那我怎么知道前面的音符呢？又是如何理解其含义的？当然，我知道是因为我记得它们。

cues.en: But if I remember them, and Husserl is very clear in that, the meaning comes from the notes being playing now and the memories of the previous one. So it's all in the present, so to say, and it can be all in the present together because there is memory. But it's more than that, because since the brain is designed by evolution to use memory to anticipate for a purpose, because it...
cues.zh: 但如果我记得它们——胡塞尔（Husserl）对此解释得很透彻——意义就来源于此刻正在演奏的音符与过去音符的记忆。所以可以说，这一切都存在于当下，而它们之所以能一同汇聚在当下，是因为有记忆。但不仅如此，因为大脑经过演化，天生就会为了特定目的利用记忆去预测，因为它……

cues.en: It's designed to try to get somewhere. That's how the linear evolution design our behavior. Then all this is strongly emotionally charged. The passage of time is not for us a rational thing to contemplate. It's something we live into.
cues.zh: 它的设计初衷就是为了达成某种目标。这正是线性演化塑造我们行为的方式。因此，这一切都带有强烈的情感色彩。时间的流逝对我们而言绝不是用来理性沉思的客体。它是我们沉浸其中的生命体验。

cues.en: We are this passage of time. We are this constant computing of time. You can think about reality without space. We can think about reality without things. It's very hard to think yourself in a reality without time. You wouldn't know how to start thinking. But the confusion is, is this because reality by itself cannot be thought without time? No. It's because our thinking cannot be thought about time.
cues.zh: 我们本身就是这段流逝的时间。我们本身就是对时间的持续计算。你可以想象一个没有空间存在的现实。我们也可以想象一个没有物质存在的现实。但你极难想象自己身处一个没有时间的现实中。你甚至不知道该从何思考起。但这里的困惑在于，这是因为现实本身脱离了时间就无法被思考吗？不是的。这是因为我们的思维脱离了时间就无法运作。

cues.en: We cannot think about time. We are a time machine, not the universe. The universe is not a time machine. The universe is just a bunch of things of events very connected to one another, which in some approximation are nicely ordered. But what we think when we think about time is the...
cues.zh: 我们无法脱离时间去思考。我们自己就是一台时间机器，而宇宙不是。宇宙并不是一台时间机器。宇宙只是一堆紧密相连的事件，在某种近似下呈现出良好的秩序。但当我们思考时间时，我们所想的其实是……

cues.en: ensemble of the memory and the anticipation that give us the sense that we are in this space, right? All of us. What is the real time? Real time is now, 10 minutes ago, my life, but then I've been to school, so I know about all the kings of England. So this long line, right? The line of the kings of England and Queens. And so I have some extended memory, which is a cultural memory. I've studied physics and cosmology, so I have this...
cues.zh: 记忆与预期的集合体，正是它让我们感觉自己存在于这个空间之中，对吧？我们所有人都是如此。什么是真实的时间？真实的时间是当下，是十分钟前，是我的整个人生；但我还上过学，所以我了解英格兰的所有君王。于是就有了这条长长的脉络，对吧？历代英格兰国王与女王的传承脉络。因此我拥有了一种延伸的记忆，一种文化层面的记忆。我学过物理学和宇宙学，所以我拥有了……

cues.en: memory longer. It's all today. It's all my knowledge today. It's all here. In the book I talk about Proust. Proust has written this fantastic novel, In Search of Lost Time. It's all about time. He says that explicitly. It's a reflection of the meaning of time. And the novel is full of stories, character, things, but the novel is presented not as...
cues.zh: 更久远的记忆。但这全都在今天。全都是我今天的知识。全都在这里。在书中我提到了普鲁斯特（Proust）。普鲁斯特写了那部了不起的小说《追忆似水年华》。它完全是关于时间的。他明确指出了这一点。这是对时间意义的反思。小说中充满了故事、人物与琐事，但小说的呈现方式并不是……

cues.en: what is happening in the world or what has happened in the world, but as the memory of the main character, whose name is probably Marcel, it's not clear the name of the main character. So all the 3,000 pages of Pluth's novel are about what's in this, you know, five inches between the years of Marcel. It's all here.
cues.zh: 世界上正在发生什么，或是世界上曾经发生过什么，而是作为主角的记忆——主角的名字大概叫马塞尔（Marcel），小说里主角的名字其实并不明确。所以普鲁斯特整整三千页的小说，讲的全都是马塞尔双耳之间那区区几英寸大脑里的东西。全都在这里。

cues.en: And that's the greatest intuition of Proust. To understand what is time for us, we have to look at the specific of our brain functioning more than the temporal structure of the universe itself. Of course, there's a relationship. I'm not saying that the temporal structure of the universe itself is irrelevant. But I'm saying that by looking only at the temporal structure of the universe, you always get the feeling that there is something missing.
cues.zh: 这就是普鲁斯特最伟大的洞见。要理解时间对我们意味着什么，与其研究宇宙本身的时间结构，不如去探究我们大脑运作的特殊机制。当然，两者是有联系的。我并不是说宇宙本身的时间结构毫无意义。但我认为，如果只盯着宇宙的时间结构，你总会觉得漏掉了什么。

cues.en: with respect to the time of our experience. And so you do metaphysical speculation about the primarity of time, which are completely wrong, because of course there's something missing, because it doesn't pertain to the fundamental structure of the universe. It pertains to the way our brain machine works. And last point, it's strongly emotionally colored. Time is not emotionally neutral to us.
cues.zh: 漏掉了关于我们亲身体验到的时间。于是你开始对时间的本质进行形而上学的思辨，而这些思辨完全是错的，因为缺失的那部分确实存在，但它并不属于宇宙的基础结构。它关乎的是我们大脑这台机器的运作方式。最后一点，它带有强烈的先验情感色彩。时间对我们来说绝非情感中立的。

cues.en: precisely because our brain is a machine designed to tell the story about the past and do something in the future. We are full of motivation. We have hunger, we have thirst, we have ambition, we have curiosity, we have love, we have hate. That's what we are before being rational beings. And this drive is the drive of the brain
cues.zh: 恰恰是因为，我们的大脑就是一台用来讲述过去、并在未来采取行动的机器。我们充满了动力。我们会饥饿、会口渴，有野心、有好奇心，会爱、也会恨。在成为理性的人之前，我们首先是这样的存在。而这种驱动力，正是大脑的驱动力——

cues.en: that, you know, control our homeostasis and struggle to make us survive and do better because evolution wants us to be like that. It's all oriented in time. It's all in time. So time is emotionally charged for us. Time is what brings us things. We want is the opening of the future, okay? And time is what is emotionally charged for us because it makes us lose things constantly all the time.
cues.zh: 它维持着我们的体内平衡，拼尽全力让我们活下去并活得更好，因为进化赋予了我们这样的使命。这一切都导向时间，都发生于时间之中。因此，时间对我们而言满载着情感。时间为我们带来所求之物，向我们敞开未来，对吧？时间之所以满载情感，也是因为它是让我们不断、永远在失去东西的原因。

cues.en: In Buddhism, there's this deep psychological inside, I think, the main truth of Buddhism. First is life is suffering, but the second is that life is suffering because we have difficulty of dealing with impermanence, with time.
cues.zh: 在佛教中，有一种极具深度的心理洞察，我认为那是佛法的核心真谛。第一是人生皆苦，而第二是，人生之所以苦，是因为我们难以面对无常，难以面对时间。

cues.en: So time is a source of our suffering. We suffer because we lose things, or because we have lost things, or because we think we will lose things. So we're going to die. So this is a quintessential source of anxiety for humans. So time is strongly colored emotionally. And why I'm saying this? Because I think if we think that this emotional side of time is a sort of fog that does not allow us to see the
cues.zh: 所以时间是我们痛苦的根源。我们受苦，是因为我们正在失去、已经失去，或者预见到自己将要失去。我们终有一死。这就是人类焦虑的根本来源。因此，时间带有极其强烈的情感色彩。我为什么要说这些？因为我认为，如果我们觉得时间的这种情感维度只是一层迷雾，遮蔽了我们去看清

cues.en: real nature of time, we are confusing ourselves because this emotional aspect of time is precisely what is deeply time for us. Time for us is this emotional connection to the event of the world that go away, that pass, that flow, that we lose. And this is the root.
cues.zh: 时间的真实本质，那我们就是在自欺欺人，因为时间的这种情感属性，恰恰构成了它对我们而言最深刻的意义。对我们来说，时间就是一种与世间万物的情感羁绊——看着它们远去、逝去、流淌，看着我们失去它们。而这正是

cues.en: of our strong sense of passing time and feeling time. It's ingrained working of our brain. This is vaguely connected to this event. It works because it's entropy, of course, because at our scale we can orient things like this. But you see, understanding time...
cues.zh: 我们感知时间流逝、体悟时间的强烈感受的根源。它是我们大脑根深蒂固的运作机制。这与发生的事件隐约相关。它之所以起作用，当然是因为熵，因为在我们的尺度上，我们可以确定这样的方向。但你看，理解时间……

cues.en: means bringing out the pieces of this layered complex object. Time is not a single thing. Time for us is not a single thing. It's all these layers that come from approximation, from disregarding aspect of nature, from thermodynamics, from our particular relation to the world, and from our...
cues.zh: 意味着要剥离出这个复杂多层对象的各个组成部分。时间并非单一的存在。对我们而言，时间不是单一之物。它包含了所有这些层次，源于近似、源于对自然某些方面的忽略、源于热力学、源于我们与世界的特殊联系，以及源于我们的……

cues.en: function of our brain, including this emotional level. Out there, the more we go general in the picture of the universe, the more time loses pieces and there is a very weak form of temporality. And in the closest to us, I think the strong emotional connection with time, the motion of time, is what time is for us. Thank you.
cues.zh: 我们大脑的功能，包括这种情感层面。在外部世界，当我们越是从宏观上去看宇宙的全貌，时间剥落的碎片就越多，只剩下一种非常微弱的时间性形式。而在离我们最近的地方，我认为正是与时间的强烈情感联系，那种时间的流动，构成了对我们而言的时间。谢谢大家。
